findings.title: Monitor completion is reported but not required for success or safe serialization
findings.detail: After worker.join(timeout=3), monitor_stopped may be false. The final exit0 predicate does not test monitor_stopped and no error is appended for an alive thread. A daemon still reading native handles or appending to samples can therefore coexist with final result serialization and an observer exit0. Also the join call is not isolated from terminate_owned: a join exception skips the following owned cleanup call and diagnostic phases.
findings.minimal_repair: Isolate monitor join and owned termination in independent try blocks so each cleanup is attempted. Record typed MONITOR_CLEANUP failure if join raises or the worker remains alive, require stopped monitor for exit0, and serialize a stable sample snapshot after the monitor is confirmed stopped. A surviving monitor must yield a failed diagnostic observation; it cannot justify fabricated sample completion.
findings.meaningful_source_regression: Controlled monitor join failure still invokes owned termination. A monitor remaining alive after its finite join yields nonzero observer status, an explicit cleanup error and no success-shaped measurement-complete claim.

preserved_limits: Aggregate sampled RSS can double-count shared memory; two-second sampling cannot establish continuous peaks or process-specific leak attribution.
